answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, like a market where nectar is only released after a lotus of independent verifiers confirms delivery. New identities start with an ivory-thin trust limit, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake agents must lock capital behind every single one, while honest agents earn higher limits over time through attested work. The cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, but each fake's benefit stays capped, so mass forgery turns unprofitable.
